thread:
alice: Quick heads-up — brought up new reranker v2 (open-model base -> distilled) on the dev stack. Did a quick goldenset run (100 canonical queries) and saw a drop in NDCG@10 vs our fp32 baseline.
ben: bummer — numbers?
alice: fp32 baseline: ndcg@10 = 0.412; int8 PTQ: ndcg@10 = 0.392. mrr dropped ~0.03.
carla: that's a sizable delta for 100 queries, could be sampling noise or formatting drift. How does the sampled eval (10k) look?
alice: sampled eval: ndcg@10 fp32=0.409 vs int8=0.404. much smaller gap.
ezra: interesting — goldenset shows larger drop than population eval. maybe goldenset has more short queries or punctuation-sensitive cases. any query/doc preproc differences?
fiona: did you run tokenizer parity check (prod vs eval harness)? we had issues where anchor docs used strip_tags earlier which nuked important tokens.
alice: good call — harness used legacy preproc (strip html + collapse whitespace), dev serving path uses keep-html=false but different strip order. I re-ran 20 failing golden queries with identical preproc and gap shrank to 0.007.
ben: so part of it is formatting. what's left could be quantization sensitivity on short contexts or top-k scoring. Can we repro at the scoring level? i.e., dump logits/topk for both runs on same inputs.
carla: yes — also check candidate-ordering and tie-breakers. Our eval harness sorts candidates by id in some tests; prod uses retrieval order which can interact with tiny score shifts.
ezra: also confirm kv-cache/batch behavior — were these runs with continuous batching enabled? batching seeds / order nondeterminism can flip near-ties.
alice: initial runs were with batching=on and deterministic=false. I'll run deterministic single-thread for the goldenset.
devbot: deploy v2-int8 started on dev-gpu-01 (job id gv-778).
alice: quick note: embedding/scoring scaling also changed between distilled model and base; I had to remove the postnorm scaling factor in the inference shim to match old scores — forgot to mention earlier.
fiona: can you paste the small repro command you used? makes it easier to reproduce locally.
alice: sure:
```
python eval_runner.py --dataset goldenset.jsonl --model rerank-v2-int8 --tokenizer-rules legacy --deterministic true --dump-topk /tmp/topk.jsonl
```
ben: after you dump topk, diff the topk ranks and the raw scores. if quant introduces monotonic rescaling we can fix with a scalar calibrator per-batch.
carla: are we using per-channel quant or per-tensor? that matters for attention layers.
alice: PTQ auto: per-tensor by default. we can try per-channel for weights > 64k params.
ezra: also run a tiny ablation: re-run those golden queries but pad context to 512 tokens (we suspect truncation edgecases). sometimes short queries produce high variance.
fiona: add a check for tokenization boundary: rare cases where trailing punctuation gets attached to token and model weight differs post-quant.
alice: agreed. I'll schedule runs: 1) deterministic single-thread int8 w/legacy preproc, 2) int8 per-channel quant, 3) int8 with padded contexts, 4) fp32 distilled (sanity). Expected turnaround ~2h on dev-gpu-01.
ben: also capture eval metadata: candidate_ordering=retrieval, shuffle_seed=42, tokenizer_config=v1, batching=off/on — put into the job env.
aldea: (typo) ignore last line.
carla: cool — once we have topk diffs, we should compute NDCG breakdown by query length buckets and by candidate-length buckets. goldenset might be skewed to short queries.
ezra: and compute per-query delta signs; if a few queries drive the full delta we can investigate those cases individually.
fiona: +1. On the tuning side, we can try a tiny calibration step: learn a per-query scalar from a tiny dev fold and apply before ranking; often fixes scale drift from quant.
alice: logging plan: I'll attach /tmp/topk.jsonl, tokenizer snapshots, and a small repro script. Will post results here when done.
devbot: job gv-778 finished: status=success, elapsed=1h48m. artifacts: s3://redwood-dev/gv-778/topk.jsonl
alice: results: deterministic int8 w/legacy preproc -> ndcg@10 0.405 (goldenset). per-channel int8 -> 0.408. padded context -> 0.407. fp32 distilled -> 0.412. So most of gap narrowed with per-channel and parity preprocessing.
ben: great — per-channel seems to help. what's the cost perf tradeoff? quant kernels per-channel can be slightly slower.
alice: perf: int8 per-tensor avg latency 42ms, per-channel 48ms, fp32 86ms. throughput similar for batch>8.
carla: acceptable trade if ndcg matches closer. can we add a tiny calibrator to recover the last few points and keep per-tensor?
fiona: maybe — try multiplicative scalar fit on a small calibration set and measure on goldenset holdout.
ezra: also add a check to the onboarding checklist: tokenizer parity + candidate ordering + deterministic seed for goldenset runs, include perf numbers. this will avoid future noisy comparisons.
alice: will update onboarding doc and add a short checklist PR.
ben: thanks — this was a concise bring-up. Will keep an eye on the integrated eval jobs later this week. :thumbsup:
carla: thanks all. final ask: please link the s3 artifacts in the PR so reviewers can eyeball topk diffs.
alice: done — PR #3482 links artifacts.
